summary: The note previews four community charity runs after September 1, 2023, each backing a different cause: cardiac health, local schools, social justice, and hunger relief. Organizers stress inclusivity and accessibility, with options for walkers, wheelchairs, strollers, relay teams and kids. The note closes by urging early registration and community participation.
one_line: Four fall 2023 local charity runs support heart health, schools, social justice and hunger while emphasizing inclusivity and accessibility for all participants.
key_facts: The Heart & Sole Marathon takes place Sunday, September 10, 2023, and is driven by local hero Janice McCormick, who has overcome heart disease.
All proceeds from the Heart & Sole Marathon support cardiac health research and rehabilitation programs.
The Heart & Sole Marathon offers a full marathon, a half-marathon, a 10-kilometer run, a 5-kilometer fun run, and a 1-mile 'Heart Walk', with the mantra "Every step counts."
The Sprint for Schools 5K is on Sunday, October 8, 2023, raising money for local underfunded schools.
Sprint for Schools 5K is organized by school teacher Michael Sanchez and is family-friendly, welcoming strollers, wheelchairs, and walkers.
The Unity Ultra is on Sunday, November 5, 2023, and covers over 50 kilometers to stand with those fighting social injustices.
The Unity Ultra was initiated by social rights advocate Lydia Hansen; participants can go at their own pace and teams can run in relays.
The Jingle Jog for Hunger is a 10K on Sunday, December 3, 2023, organized by food pantry coordinator Frank Thompson.
Jingle Jog participants are invited to wear holiday costumes, and families can join the shorter 'Santa's Elves Fun Run'.
Each Jingle Jog for Hunger registration results in a food donation to local shelters.
All the events are slated to occur after September 1, 2023, and organizers aim to include participants regardless of physical ability.
Participants are encouraged to register early, begin training, and spread the word.
